#4154. "What if Larian had shut down after Divine Divinity?": Star Trek Online exec scorns publishers who close teams like BioWare in favour of "AAA veteran" start-ups and AI "magic beans"

It's like "setting fire to millions of dollars of property and equipment"

Breaking up established game development teams in favour of "AAA veteran" start-ups and "magic bean" technologies is like "setting fire to millions of dollars of property and equipment", in the words of Star Trek Online executive producer Thomas Marrone. He thinks it's "wildly irresponsible and self-sabotaging", and that videogame company shareholders should be absolutely furious about it.

Marrone's comments come in response to EA closing BioWare yesterday, but he takes aim at closures and layoffs across the industry. He notes that many of the most successful teams owe their accomplishments to lessons learned from screw-ups, and suggests that if big game publishers just want "number to go up", they should get out of the game-making trade and pour all their cash into investment funds.

"One of the most insightful comments about game development came from a former boss," Marrone wrote on Bluesky this morning. "He said 'Making a game is like starting a band. You can’t throw money at a new studio with random AAA veterans and expect it to crank out a hit.' A good game needs a vision. A good game needs a good team to build it. A good team needs chemistry to work well together. Team chemistry needs years of collaboration to gel. There are certainly 'rockstars' and leaders who are anchors for their team, but they need to have that chemistry and trust with everyone around them to be truly effective.

"The AAA philosophy seems to be to hire four random musicians and expect them to become the Beatles overnight," Marrone went on. "When it does happen: well, we have the songs now, we can just hire different musicians to record new songs when we want another album. It’s truly insane and shows a fundamental misunderstanding of the collaborative creative process at the heart of making games.

"Most studios that generate an overnight hit are actually on the 3rd or 4th title," he said. "Blizzard, Larian, Arrowhead, these places had several games under their belts before their first true blockbuster. Like George RR Martin they had been grinding XP for years before becoming a household name. The current AAA Publisher practice of disbanding studios, even if they ship a game successfully, is so counterintuitive to their own financial future it boggles my mind.

"Like if I were a major shareholder I would be livid," Marrone observed. "This is wanton destruction of these publishers’ most precious assets. It’s like literally setting fire to millions of dollars of property and equipment. It’s wildly irresponsible and self-sabotaging. If big game publishers just want number to go up, fire everyone and just invest it all in mutual funds or something. If you don’t want to actually make a product, and you don’t want to build a business around making a product, just liquidate your assets and stop pretending you want to make anything."

Marrone has been at Cryptic Studios for 16 years, starting out as an associate graphics designer. "I've worked on one game through that whole career, which means I've seen lots of leaders come and go, and lots of versions of the company and the game as it grew, shrunk, and changed," he noted.

Cryptic themselves were founded in 2000, and are also known for Champions Online, City of Heroes and Neverwinter. They've been through a lot of upheaval lately. Cryptic were acquired by (*dread bell tolls*) publishing conglomerate Embracer in 2021, during the latter's early-Covid-era campaign to absorb half the industry. When Embracer belatedly acknowledged that all of their acquisitions had left them up shit creek without a paddle, Cryptic Studios were among the many subsidiaries who had to lay off staff. Then, Embracer sold them to Project Golden Arc, a new company formed by former Star Trek Online publishers Arc and XD Inc, publishers of Torchlight: Infinite and Heartopia.

I'm not sure how many of Cryptic's founding staff are still there, but Marrone makes it sound like they've done a fair job of keeping their teams together. "I have very personal experience working on a team that has gone through all the corpo speak stages 'forming, storming, norming, and performing,'" he wrote. "It can take Y E A R S to get to that final stage. When you do, it's awesome. People are 2, 3, 4x as effective as when they start. But it just. takes. Time."

"It takes time to build a team," Marrone went on. "It takes shared experiences. It takes shared wins AND shared losses. What if Larian had shut down after Divine Divinity? What if Arrowhead had shut down after Magicka? What if Hello Games had shuttered after the initial launch of No Man's Sky? These studios have all had ups and downs but they were given time to grow and learn and their teams got better and better. Not to say those teams were static, but certainly there was a continuity and culture that informed their biggest successes.

"And when you look at the arc of a studio like Bioware, you can begin to see how important it is to keep the teams healthy, how important it is to keep those rockstars and leaders together with the teams that know them," he said. "Mass Effect is a great game. Mass Effect 2 is one of the best games of all time.

"In my current position I understand the pressure of leadership when millions of dollars and hundreds of salaries are at stake," Marrone concluded. "I understand the drive to find a magic bean like NFTs or GenAI or whatever is trending on LinkedIn this week. There's got to be a 'trick.' We've got to find a 'trick.' But." Marrone ends the thread by reiterating the need to "nurture and empower your team".

We've heard plenty of common-sensical commentary like this from other senior devs of late. In April, Bit Reactor boss and former XCOM developer Greg Foertsch spoke to Julian about how he and other Firaxis managers "kept the team together" across development of Sid Meier's Railroads, XCOM: Enemy Unknown, and XCOM 2.

We've also recently seen a number of new "AAA veteran" startups come and go, as investors take fright after an initial buzz of interest during the Covid lockdown period. Former BioWare manager Casey Hudson launched a new studio in 2021 only to shutter the company in 2024. Former Mass Effect and Dragon Age scribe Mac Walters similarly launched a company in 2023, only for publishers NetEase to pull funding a year later. There are going to be a lot more BioWare veterans in the wilds this year, joining many thousands laid off by the likes of Microsoft and Ubisoft.

#4153. Never one to lag behind HSR and ZZZ, Genshin Impact will introduce its own new pink-haired animal-themed girl in Version Luna 6

Plus Mondstadt is expanding yet further north in Genshin Impact's Luna 6 update.

Today’s Genshin Impact Special Program has wrapped up, and it’s brought us some big news about the next major update. Luna 6 is the next phase in the action RPG’s story, titled Song of the Welkin Moon: Rondo - Augured Homecoming.

It’s set to arrive on April 8, bringing with it a tonne of new content, including a big expansion to the original region of Mondstadt.

As part of this new update, Mondstadt’s northern parts expand with new areas. The new Dornman Port is one thing, but the most exciting is the Temple of Space. This floating structure is home to Asmoday fragments, and is made up of different realms inspired by Liyue, Sumeru, and various other civilizations from around Teyvat. Launching with the update is a new mechanic that lets you manipulate the space to reveal hidden paths containing secrets.

If you take the time to explore, you’ll find a lot to there to learn about Asmoday, Ruler of Space. There’s a new boss to take on in the temple, too: Watcher: Fallen Vigil.

The only new character in Luna 6 is Linnea, who continues the current trend within HoYoverse games of focussing heavily on cute pink-haired animal-themed girls. Linnea is a 5-Star Geo Bow user who can really work with parties made up of Lunar-Crystallize characters, with her big gimmick being the ability to turn Hydro-Crystallize reactions into Lunar-Crystallize reactions.

Linnea has a companion, Lumi, who allows her to increase the Lunar-Crystallize damage she deals, while also lowering her enemies’ Geo resistance. Linnea can also deliver either off-field Geo damage or a Lunar-Crystallize reaction hit with her Elemental Skill.

Beyond that, she can heal the party using her Elemental Burst. If you take Linnea with you as you explore, she can help you discover rare animals, thanks to her innate naturalist abilities.

This update will also see Chasca get her first-ever rerun, and you’ll be able to roll for her in the first phase of Event Wishes. The second phase will feature no new characters and instead focus on Nefer and Lauma. There’s going to be another Chronicled Wish banner, this time specifically for Fontaine characters.

You can look forward to a few other new arrivals in Luna 6, including The Nod-Krai Trade Expo, some quality of life updates to Miliastra Wonderland to up the number of players in each lobby, not to mention various other UI changes.

Catch up on the latest Genshin Impact codes before you jump for some freebies.

#4152. Feature: Threads Of Time - The Best Ocarina References & Easter Eggs In The Wider Zelda Series

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a masterpiece. An enduring classic that set the standard, and often the template, for virtually every single action-adventure game that followed in its footsteps.

A cultural touchstone for a generation, there are references to it littered throughout its gaming descendants and beyond, but there will now be an entirely new generation of player preparing to embark upon this chapter of the Zelda story - a good chunk of whom will have only experienced a Zelda title post-N64 (or no Zelda at all).

Which begs the question: will all those many, many references finally fall into place for them, like a well-constructed block-pushing puzzle?

It would be impossible to track it across all of gaming, of course, so instead we have listed some of our favourite and most obscure callbacks to the Ocarina of Time in the mainline Zelda games that came after. Grab a fresh cup of Lon Lon Milk for the read - there are a lot of them…

A bit of a false start, this, as essentially the entire game is a reference, utilising many of the same assets as its predecessor. But the story confirms Link isn’t the only person to make the trip from Hyrule to Termina - the game’s antagonist, Skull Kid, and The Happy Mask Salesman both recognise Link and mention his previous exploits.

Anju’s Grandmother is Granny in OoT, a different character who runs the potion shop and strokes a tiger cub in Hyrule. The tiger doesn’t make the jump to Termina, but there is a tiger portrait adorning the back of her wheelchair.

The 3DS adds a few more details. In the fishing hole, you can catch Lord Chapu-Chapu, a reference to OoT's giant fish/dungeon using a miniaturised version of its character model. And Ganondorf may be absent, but you can find a stuffed plushie of his horse on the floor in Romani’s Ranch.

After OoT released and canonically established itself as the Sealing War referenced in A Link to the Past’s manual, the opening text was changed in the GBA re-release from ‘seven wise men’ to ‘seven sages’ to directly reference the sages encountered in Ocarina of Time. Neat!

Wind Waker is positively awash with references, so let’s tackle some obscure ones.

A lot of musical themes, phrases and variations are used, and though Outset Island, where Link starts his adventure, has its own theme, it features a phrase lifted straight out of Kokiri Forest.

The Water Spirit Jabun’s theme is a callback to the theme inside Lord Jabu-Jabu (minus his tummy grumbles); however, a cheeky nod to the Great Deku Tree lies within the Sacred Shrines dotted around the great sea. The theme inside these is a variation on Link’s first OoT dungeon.

Speaking of smaller islands, the Goddess Statues on the Triangle Islands bear inscriptions on their bases which translate to Din’s Fire, Nauru’s Love, and Farore’s Wind - the spells Link can summon in OoT.

Ganondorf and the Great Deku Tree are canonically the same characters (the latter having grown from his sprout), but perhaps the most wild callback is a Rito named Koboli. The Nintendo Gallery within Wind Waker states that he is descended from three generations of Postmen and had an ancestor who was one. Take a close look and you can see that his face is modelled after the postman in Majora's Mask, who is of course the running man in OoT.

The Nintendo Gallery houses some more of our favourite easter eggs. There are bottles of Lon Lon Milk as well as the Bunny Hood and Keaton Mask up on the wall, but just behind the desk to the left is an unfinished bust of a character - the face shape and hairstyle clearly indicate this is a bust of the Kokiri sage, Saria.

That’s far from the only nod to the sages. The Master Sword chamber’s stained glass windows are pretty well known, but Wind Waker’s Kokiri sage Fado is also named after the girl who sits above the shop in Kokiri Forest. His role as the Sage of Wind is another nod to OoT, as the Forest Temple was originally intended to be the Wind Temple, something you can still see in the game by the medallion featuring a fan blade pattern.

The other sage, Medli, is a descendant of the Zora. Like Ruto was to Lord Jabu-Jabu, Medli is the attendant to the Rito's deity, Valoo, and the dungeon has Link haul Medli around above his head, just as you did with Princess Ruto.

To finish on a fun one, Wind Waker once again gives Link the ability to use a glass bottle to deflect Phantom Ganon’s energy balls back at him during Dead Man’s Volley, just like you could in OoT!

There seems to be a pattern of the top-down 2D games paying greater tribute to A Link to the Past. Nevertheless, Minish Cap does feature a few OoT nods.

There are a couple of audio callbacks that are really tricky to catch - the Kokiri Forest theme is remixed here to form the Hyrule Town music, while Link’s voice also samples child Link from OoT.

Popular characters return. As does Dampé. And there are some carpenters and builders in Minish Cap that share the design aesthetic from the carpenters on the N64.

A nice thematic nod is the set-piece routine of rescuing Princess Zelda after battling Vaati, only to have to escort her out as the castle crumbles down around you both. Subtle, but undeniable.

The obvious one here is that the overworld map very closely resembles the Ocarina's Hyrule. The Forest, Death Mountain, Lake Hylia, and Gerudo Desert all return and are more or less where you’d expect them to be, though you may not have caught this if, like so many of us, you played Twilight Princess on the Wii first (it mirrored the game world so East became West).

Three of the game’s Light Spirits — Eldin, Lanayru, and Faron — are named after the Hylian Goddesses, who themselves are depicted in a carving above Zelda’s throne portraying the creation myth from OoT's cutscene.

Ganondorf is, yet again, the same Ganondorf you fought in OoT and there’s a few other cool character nods, too. Skull Kid in the Lost Woods is accompanied by Saria’s Song, the same piece you taught Skull Kid in OoT, and Majora’s Mask antagonist. A popular fan theory is that he returned to Hyrule and, possibly being an immortal creature, agreed to guard the Master Sword for his good friend who helped him in Termina.

The fishing hole in Hyrule is run by Hena, the descendant of the owner of the fishing hole in OoT, of whom there is a black-and-white portrait behind the desk. She even has the same itchy back affliction shared by her forefather.

The White Wolf/Heroes Shade is the deceased, spectral reincarnation of the Hero of Time from OoT, which explains why the Howling Stones it gets you to use feature both the Prelude of Light and the Requiem of Spirit.

These are many more musical references, including the Serenade of Water playing whenever you talk to Rutella, Queen of the Zora, but she and her son, Prince Ralis, also sport necklaces featuring a pendant that resembles the Zora Sapphire.

Oh, and we can once again enjoy a game of Dead Man’s Volley with an empty bottle. Huzzah!

Where Wind Waker was stuffed with OoT callbacks, its DS sequels are substantially less so. However, a fairy companion returns for this game and shares the same design as Navi. Gossip Stones made an appearance, too.

The A Spirit Opens the Way track is a variation of the Creation of Hyrule theme from OoT - not one that’s sampled often. I also maintain that Spirit Tracks' Dungeon Gauntlet theme is a remix of the Battle theme that plays during the fight with Gohma, but someone with a better ear might disagree.

Being a game that launched on the 25th anniversary of the Zelda series, Skyward Sword has some choice OoT nods.

Just like the DS pair of games, the Gossip Stones are back, but this time they share a secret with OoT: flinging a bomb at one will cause it to count down and launch into the air like a rocket.

Loftwings, the bird companions of the game, are a callback/forward to OoT’s iconic Hylian Shield - in particular Link’s red Loftwing, which matches the hue of the bird on the shield’s front.

A strong visual nod occurs once the Isle of the Goddess falls into the Sealed Grounds. Looking up into the ceiling of the newly formed Sealed Temple reveals a mural of the Triforce surrounded by the sage medallions, which in itself bears a striking resemblance to the Chamber of Sages Link returns to after clearing a temple.

In this game, Zelda hands over a precious, magical instrument to Link before her own power awakens later on in the game, just like Zelda in OoT.

Lastly, a puzzle and thematic callback. The Lanayru Mining Facility contains a puzzle where you have to hit three switches in a specific order — 2, 3, 1 — a reference to the final puzzle of OoT’s Great Deku Tree. “23 is number 1!”

A few characters pop up here, with Dampé appearing again, not once, but twice. He’s his own parallel in both Hyrule and Lorule.

Hyrule’s unnamed Milk Bar owner also bears a striking resemblance to Talon, while his Lorule counterpart looks suspiciously like Ingo.

Two pieces of art reference OoT: a painting of a fairy design like Navi’s adorning the wall of the Stylish Woman’s House, while a small, yellowish Ocarina is on Link's wall. Easy to miss, as you need to merge into the wall to find them.

If you dash into a wall within the level lobby, there’s a chance it will drop a purple ball down. Give it a whack with your sword and you have a chance of hearing the Lost Woods theme, Zelda’s Lullaby, the Lon Lon Ranch theme or Kakariko’s Windmill theme. They only play while you juggle the ball with sword hits - once it hits the floor, it’s done!

My favourite, though, is that Link is assigned voice clips from one of four Zelda games when you create a save file. So there’s a 25% chance you’ll be hearing the guttural shouts of OoT Link while you play.

Breath of the Wild's vast map is heaving with references to other Zelda games. There’s some obvious callbacks like Ruto Lake, Mido Swamp, and Mount Nabooru, but perhaps the best callback is Koukot Plateau by the Gerudo Desert - named, fittingly, as a portmanteau of Kotake and Koume.

Eldin, Faron, and Lanayru have been used in reference to the Goddesses before, but the dragons Dinraal, Farosh, and Naydra are also named after OoT’s deities.

The Temple of Time on the Great Plateau is the classic structure from OoT, even playing the same theme inside, but a sneakier callback lies within the Ranch Ruins just south of Hyrule Castle, which perfectly mirrors the race track and layout of Lon Lon Ranch.

Some of the clothing and weapons in the game, particularly the DLC sets, straight up lift costumes from OoT, but a sneakier nod is the design of the Forest Dweller's Sword, based on the Kokiri Sword, and is even clearer to see in the upcoming remake.

And my favourite costume nod doesn’t belong to Link. Hudson, a man who builds houses from the ground up, is modelled on the carpenters in OoT.

There’s plenty of musical references, too, including one you can see but not hear. Above the throne in Hyrule Castle, there’s a Triforce surrounded by concentric rings with round dots placed along them. On closer inspection, these rings actually form a musical stave, with the dots being the notes for Zelda’s Lullaby that you learned in OoT. Incredible nod.

An incredibly faithful remake of the Game Boy original that predates OoT, the Switch version nevertheless manages to add a few nods.

Dampé is back. At this point it feels like he’s in more games than Link?

When fighting Shadow Nightmare, the ability to play Dead Man’s Volley with Agahnim’s Shadow has been retroactively added, too.

Building on the incredible reference work of BOTW, Link can now hum any of the following while cooking: Saria’s Song, Epona’s Song, or the Song of Storms, while the House theme returns for Link’s home.

The flute player Pyper raises his legs to the side in turn as he plays, a direct callback to the flute-playing skull kids in the Lost Woods.

Cutscenes deliberately evoke previous OoT ones here. Zelda’s turn and gasp in the opening, with her right hand to her mouth, is an homage to her seeing Link for the first time in OoT, while the memory A Show of Fealty mirrors what Zelda sees through the window in that very same scene - Ganondorf kneeling before the King while swearing a false oath.

Though not named, Ganondorf is also flanked by Kotake and Koume in the above and other scenes, distinguishable by the gems on their forehead and the cloths on their shoulder matching their OoT headbands.

Some conceptual nods include Ganondorf being imprisoned and sealed by seven sages, while the adventure sees Hyrule Castle raised up high above a red, ominous pit, just as it is once Link travels into the future in Ocarina of Time.

Echoes of Wisdom’s opening cutscene deliberately evokes the climax of OoT (which itself evoked past games) before switching things up, with Zelda trapped in a purple crystal and held aloft, but the whole game also heavily references the creation of myth from OoT while expanding upon it.

Kakariko Village, although appearing in several 2D Zelda games, specifically features a windmill, a graveyard, and a well (although it is covered) for the first time since OoT.

So that’s it: our favourite and most obscure Ocarina of Time nods, references, and easter eggs across the Zelda series.

There are many others, of course, and in other games. The Oracle duo, for instance, are packed with characters from Ocarina of Time - most notably giving human form to the Golden Goddesses for the first time, while also fleshing out Kotake and Koume. Elsewhere, Kaepora Gaebora, Malon and Talon, and Dampé (of all people) returned in Four Swords Adventures. As did Epona! Curiously also split into four, somehow.

There are so many references that this article was literally double the word count on draft one! But which reference is your favourite? Is there another we should’ve included? If so, give us a ‘Hey, Listen!’ in the comments below.

And before we go, a big shoutout to Zeltik, DPadGamer, A Dan in Time, Triforce Times, DidYouKnowGaming, Zelda Dungeon, Zelda Wiki, and Kevin Armes Music for their incredible work cataloguing Easter Eggs across the Zelda series.

George is a stage and screen actor and voiceover artist with a deep love of gaming and all things Nintendo. His writing has appeared on Nintendo Life and Time Extension, and he's the host of NintenDormant.

#4151. Blizzard Is Getting Our Hopes Up Again For World Of Warcraft On Xbox

One of Xbox's biggest releases of 2026 isn't actually releasing on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S - it's Blizzard's World of Warcraft: Forever, which is still a PC exclusive launching on November 5th.

That said, we've seen signs that Blizzard might be pushing towards a native Xbox release in the future, as they've implemented native controller support for WoW: Forever meaning it'll be playable on devices like the ROG Xbox Ally.

And, in a recent interview with GamesRadar, World of Warcraft Vice President Holly Longdale appeared to tease that the franchise will end up on Xbox consoles eventually, even if it's not in the immediate future.

I put it to Holly Longdale: Is World of Warcraft: Forever launching as a PC-exclusive a missed opportunity?

"What you just described is really what we're after. Play it wherever you want and, at some point,on whatever you want. But the first leg of that journey is getting gamepads working really well with World of Warcraft, and we thought Forever was the perfect place to start. Looking at where things are going when we hear about Project Helix et cetera, I think platforms will be a bit more ubiquitous," says Longdale.

As you can see, the WoW VP teases Xbox Project Helix in her reply here, suggesting that bringing World of Warcraft to a device that already supports PC games will make things much easier for Blizzard in the future.

Still, she clearly also states that the idea is to eventually allow for World of Warcraft "on whatever you want", and the first step is to implement gamepad support that works "really well". Later in the interview, she also mentions that the work on controllers will allow players "flexibility that I think goes beyond consoles".

We'll have to wait and see what happens, but all signs are pointing towards a future where we'll be playing World of Warcraft on an Xbox console eventually - it might not be the Series X or S, but it should at least be on Project Helix.

#4150. Half-Life 3 speculation reignited by Valve dev mentioning three sweet little rumored codenamey letters amid technical chat about video game noises

Wake up. There's Half-Life 3 chatter occurring again. This time because, about an hour into a panel about sounds in video games, a Valve composer has uttered three eyebrow-raising letters. HLX. In an industry rife with acronyms, what's so special about this one? Well, it's a rumoured codename for the next entry in the aforementioned series about a man with a crowbar, for one.

"Basically, that's one of the three pieces that come together to make HDR that you can easily optimise," Valve music designer Mike Morasky said during a panel at GameSoundCon, answering a regular old question about the techincal ins and out of managing sound in games. The panel had been running for about an hour when he said this, so clearly nothing that'd get people out of their seats was in the offing.

"In fact, I think Deadlock has their own version of HDR," he continued. "HLX has its own version, so on and so forth." AHA, voices screamed around the world. He said the thing. HLX, in case you're not on top of the list of acronyms that should set you off yapping about Valve games, previously appeared in a data string from a Counter-Strike 2 update and looks like it could turn out to be a codename for a future game from Gabe and co. That's going off Half-Life: Alyx's codename having been HLVR.

If it was HLXXX, I imagine one would have to assume it to be a possible codename for a Gordon Freeman sex tape or a Half-Life collaboration with Vin Diesel, star of the 2002 film XXX. I don't know about you, but either would excite me greatly.

Morasky's co-panelist David Feise doesn't look to have been subtle in sarcastically pointing out the former's slip of the tongue to him via some cheeky whispering while the two were still up in stage. Morasky also looks to have plenty of form for this sort of tongue slippage in relation to HLX.

Does any of this tell us anything other than potentially confirming once more that Half-Life 3 exists? No, but hey, it's something. One thing we do know is that ex-Valve writer Chet Faliszek has said that he wouldn't be interested in helping pen a Half-Life 3 if indeed one is hiding in the ether to catch out musicians whose mouths sometimes move faster than their brains (as happens to all of us).

#4149. Phoenix Cyclops Is Available Now as Marvel Tokon Receives Major PS5 Patch

The first post-launch DLC character for Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls is now available. Phoenix Cyclops joins the fun today, 2nd November 2026, and he's accompanied by a major game update that makes a ton of improvements.

Those who own the Year 1 Pass will already have access to Phoenix Cyclops, but he's also available as a standalone purchase, costing $7.99/£6.49.

There are also a couple of premium costumes available for purchase. There's a "Classic" blue and yellow outfit for Cyclops, while Hulk gets a Joe Fixit costume. They each sell for $4.99/£3.99.

As mentioned, Phoenix Cyclops brings with him a major game update, free for all players, that fixes and improves the overall experience.

Improvements have been implemented regarding online play and cross-play with the PC version which should make online multiplayer more stable.

There are also fixes and updates to Training mode, some Character Lessons, and numerous characters.

Probably the biggest thing, though, is a pretty big change to certain game mechanics, mostly focused around assists.

In a nutshell, developer Arc System Works has reduced the frequency you can summon and tag into allies, forcing players to play neutral/with a singular character at times and to improve legibility during a match.

The patch notes are extensive — you can read the whole lot through the link if you're interested.

#4148. Caleb's third Myth has finally arrived in Love and Deepspace, and it's good news for all the husbandbro fans out there

Love and Deepspace has kicked off a new event, squarely built around Caleb's new Memory Pair.

Love and Deepspace’s latest update is here, adding a new Memory Pair for Caleb. The event is dubbed Ghosts' Final March, and it’s available now as part of a new Limited Wish Pool, as it has always worked.

The new Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

Alongside the big new Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

If you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the new Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

The Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the new update. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

After you unlock Caleb’s Netherlord Companion, you may want to fight alongside him to get another 4-Star Memory for free. You’ll need to challenge the the Rehearsal Stage to do so, and your first clear is guaranteed to get you the Duskshard Lotus Memory.

If you’re new to Love and Deepspace, or you simply want a refresher, we’ve put together a guide to help you wrap your head around Myths; how they work and how to unlock them. Banners are also an important part of any gacha game, Love and Deepspace included, so here’s how banners work, and what the current and next banners are.

#4147. Helldivers 3 "only makes sense" if it’s so unlike Helldivers 2 "that both games can exist side by side", says Arrowhead boss, discussing their new prototype game

95% of studio still on Helldivers 2, with a "small team" on the next game

Arrowhead Game Studios will only make a Helldivers 3 if it's lightyears apart in style from Helldivers 2, or if Helldivers 2's playercount falls through the floor. This is my takeaway, at least, from a recent chat with Johan Pilestedt, chief creative officer, in which Pilestedt touched briefly on the studio's next unannounced game, while assuring me that there are still no plans for a Helldiver threequel.

According to Pilestedt, 95% of the studio is focused on Helldivers 2, with a "small team" now prototyping Arrowhead's next game. They currently have around 150 people on the books. "Studio-wise, we want to grow on our own terms and know when to stop," Pilestedt commented over email, noting that "plenty of teams hit big and immediately double their size".

As for the prospect of Helldivers 3, Pilestedt is wary of dividing the audience while Helldivers 2 still has a following, commenting that "for now, my view is that a sequel resets everything and forces players to start over", whereas "a continuation turns the game into a lifelong hobby, like LEGO or Warhammer". In what probably isn't a sign that he's getting David Lynch to direct the next Warbonds video, he framed Helldivers 2 "as a 'third space,' a community where people can spend a huge amount of their time, but equally one that players can go away from for months or years and still find fun and community when they come back." For context, Helldivers 2's Steam live playercount as of writing is 47,097, which isn't chart-topping but seems fairly respectable for a two-year-old game; this doesn't include console players, of course.

"Some studios can treat players like a short-term cash grab," Pilestedt went on. "We see players as the actual engine of the game: they're the ones bringing in friends, making memes, and keeping the game alive. When you have an active community doing that, you don’t need a sequel.

"The industry is panicking because the old live-service tricks don’t work anymore," he said. "And the biggest competitor to a Helldivers 3 would be Helldivers 2. It only makes sense to make a distinct sequel if it’s so different that both games can exist side by side. For now, making Helldivers 2 better every day makes way more sense than throwing away its momentum."

Pilestedt didn't spell out what he meant by the industry panicking, but I assume he's referring to all the live service game cancellations of late. 'Live service' in general – aka, turning games into platforms from which 'rents' can be extracted, be it an optional cosmetic purchase or a subscription - has become something of a cussword among players who'd rather their games were less online, habit-forming and, well, landlordy.

The intrigue here, for me, is just how different Helldivers 3 would need to be to stand apart from its predecessor. Helldivers 2 is a very different game from the original Helldivers, swapping the old top-down view for third-person gunnery with a greater emphasis on physics and credible weapon handling. Where should they go next?

I'm not sure Helldivers would be entertaining as a first-person shooter – so much of the game's beguiling daftness depends on seeing your character. I could well imagine a Helldivers RTS, but that'd probably be a spin-off project. There are other directions they could take within the third-person shooter genre that might change the feel while supporting the game's brash and callous dystopian humour. God, I almost typed the words "Helldivers battle royale" there. Close one!

#4146. The Petit Planet beta is coming back with new updates, but you still need to hope for an invite

If you've been missing Petit Planet since it was last available to play, you'll be happy to know that HoYoverse is hosting another test soon.

It’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next big test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse announced today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is big news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

The only bit of bad news here is that this remains a closed beta. You’re still encouraged to sign up on the official website, but you’re not guaranteed access. HoYoverse said that only a portion of players who sign up will be invited to the upcoming beta.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

#4144. Xbox Suddenly Has Two Vice City Games Releasing In Mid-November

This one's based on Zelda with GTA influences!

What do you do if you've got a GTA-inspired game set to release around the same time as GTA 6? You schedule it for the day before, of course! That's exactly what's happening in the case of Vice: Magic City Mayhem.

This game is officially coming to Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S on November 18th, 2026 - a day before the release of GTA 6 on November 19th. As you can see, Vice: Magic City Mayhem goes all-in on the same style of artwork as the Rockstar Games epic, but the game itself couldn't really be more different.

Instead, Vice: Magic City Mayhem is described as a "top-down 8-bit retro action/adventure game inspired by Zelda with a Vice City theme". It essentially seems like what you'd get if you took old-school Zelda and combined it with Vice City.

Step into the shoes of Dutch, one of Magic City’s most feared enforcers, on a thrilling and dangerous quest to rescue your one true love, Sophie. Navigate through the chaos of wild nightclubs, scenic beaches, and raptor-infested yachts in this raunchy, high-stakes adventure.

In Vice: Magic City Mayhem, we blend the best of both worlds—drawing inspiration from the immersive exploration, intense combat, and mind-bending puzzles of Zelda, alongside the outrageous storylines, vibrant world-building, and dark humor of Vice City.

What's particularly interesting about this is that it started life as a Kickstarter project last year, securing $13,278 worth of funding alongside a $10,000 goal. Some of the developers working on the project have worked at the likes of EA and Telltale Games as well, so there's every chance it's going to be worth picking up.

Let's see how it goes, eh? We just admire the bravery of releasing right next to GTA 6 in November with a game that seems similar but actually offers something very different, and here's hoping that bold bet will ultimately pay off.

If you're interested, Vice: Magic City Mayhem is available to pre-order on the Xbox Store for £12.49 / $14.99.

Roam the gritty streets of Magic City, facing off against a colorful, eccentric cast of enemies and bosses, all while chasing down your elusive "Princess" in a city where danger is around every corner. #4143. Arkane survival negotiations reportedly seeing "several forms of takeover" considered ahead of November deadline, as Marvel's Blade production nears end

217 jobs are on the line at the studio, report claims

Update: A Microsoft rep has told PC Gamer that the company have "extended the consultation period by one additional month as we explore options, including finding a partner to support [Arkane] through the development work still ahead." "This is a defined extension," they added, "and we remain committed to keeping the Works Council informed throughout the process."

So, Microsoft's consultation with Arkane's Social and Economic Committee now looks set to roll on until December 13th. Though, as we previously noted, the Printemps Écologique union have said that this consultation deadline isn't the deadline by which Arkane need to have found a buyer, with the setting of the latter deadline being one of the things that needs to take place as part of the ongoing negotiations.

Negotiations over the future of Dishonored and Deathloop developers Arkane Lyon are reportedly seeing "several forms of takeover" considered as a November deadline looms for the divorce Xbox set in motion back in July. French law makes the process of shuttering or chucking away studios a lot harder for companies like Microsoft than it is elsewhere in the world, hence Arkane's fate still being up in the air while production work on Marvel's Blade nears completion according to the report.

French publication Le Monde are behind this paywalled report on how the negotiations between the two sides are going. They note that due to a French law brought in as of 2014, companies with more than 1000 staff have to search for a buyer for three months before they can throw up their hands and shut up shop. In the case of Arkane Lyon, the report says 217 jobs are at risk.

The deadline for these consultations with Arkane's Social and Economic Committee (via Gematsu) is November 13th, though Arkane have longer than that to pin down a buyer for the studio - speaking to RPS, a Printemps Écologique union representative clarified that the exact date is being negotiated and subject to change.

The Le Monde report also cites a representative of Printemps Écologique, who along with the Syndicat des Travailleureuses du Jeu Video (STJV) union seemingly aren't too happy with Microsoft's attitude throughout the process so far.

Microsoft have told Le Monde that they're "actively seeking a partner to support the next phase of development and enable the commercialisation of the [Marvel’s Blade] project". According to a union rep cited in the report, the superhero game is "nearing the end" of production, with the unions understandably backing Arkane's work and hoping that it will see the light of day.

Xbox wrote as part of an announcement of layoffs in September - the second of multiple waves in a mass chopping that still isn't over as of writing - that they expected consultation over how Arkane will move forward "to continue through the end of the year".

Solidarity to all of the developers at Arkane and here's hoping these negotiations do end with a result that keeps the maximum amount of them in work and making the games they want to make.

This article has been updated to clarify that the deadline for Arkane finding a buyer isn't the same as the deadline for the consultation period.

#4142. Final Fantasy Resonance Producer Had to Fight Square Enix Execs Who Wanted Cheap Port of Dead Mobile Game

Final Fantasy Resonance has seemingly gone down really, really well with fans of the franchise — and so it's surprising to hear that Square Enix's leadership were apparently against the idea of the game.

Resonance is very much a callback to classic Final Fantasy in terms of gameplay and structure; some would go as far to argue that it's just what the property needs at this point.

The recently released and highly rated RPG is built on the bones of Final Fantasy Brave Exvius — the mobile gacha game that was shut down back in 2024.

However, Resonance reworks entire systems to ensure that everything functions as you'd expect of a traditional Final Fantasy adventure. After playing it myself for review, it's clear that the development team put a lot of effort into essentially remaking Exvius.

But according to project producer Keisuke Nakashima, his higher-ups wanted a simple port of Exvius rather than the extensive adaptation that we ended up with.

Review Final Fantasy Resonance (PS5) - Square's Series Returns to Its Roots to Fantastic Effect

He told Bloomberg (via Nintendo Everything): "Initially there was some resistance to the idea from Square Enix executives [...] I didn’t want to go down that route. I wanted to create an original version for consoles that was a full-blown gameplay experience.”

The suggestion is that a straightforward port would have cost much less to produce. At the time of writing, we don't know how well Resonance has sold.

Still, I'm glad Nakashima held his ground, because I'm not even sure how an Exvius port would have worked in the first place. It certainly wouldn't have hit like Resonance does.

Have you been playing Final Fantasy Resonance? What do you think of it? Protect those crystals at all costs in the comments section below.

#4141. Nintendo Shares Ocarina Of Time Switch 2 Design Sketches

The latest Ask the Developer interviews are positively packed with interesting tidbits about the making of Ocarina of Time on Switch 2. One such story is all about the game's reimagined visuals, which Nintendo was even kind enough to share some initial sketches of.

According to Art Director Aya Shida, the team was consciously fighting a battle between making the game more realistic with the improved power of the Switch 2, and retaining the spirit of the original — a somewhat dark world, filled with weird characters. She therefore relied on phrases like “a puppet-show feel” and “the analogue feel of practical effects films” during development to reflect the goal: "both create a convincing sense that the characters truly exist within their respective fantasy worlds".

When it came to these characters, the team wanted to preserve their "familiar presence" first and foremost, before adding "designs unique to this game" on top. Hence, we end up with a recognisable Child Link, but with far more costume bells and whistles attached.

Here's a handful of the design sketches themselves, so you can see how the characters were initially conceptualised:

The same can be said for the game's iconic maps. "We didn't want to change the feel of each location or the way the locations connected with one another," Director HokWai Ng says in the interview, "both of which are so characteristic of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time". The team therefore went back to one of the artists who had worked on illustrations for the N64 original, and asked them to draw a new map for the game.

We even get to see this very sketch, too:

Such an approach resulted in the style we see today, which, we must say, has grown on us over the last few months — it really is quite the looker, eh?

One thing that is already rubbing some people up the wrong way, mind you, is how the game seemingly opts for SMAA over DLSS for its upscaling and anti-aliasing tech. Footage of the game's preloaded intellectual property notice has been doing the rounds on social media, where AMD FSR 1.0 and SMAA are listed under third-party technologies over Nvidia's DLSS. The same approach was taken on Donkey Kong Bananza, we should point out.

Based on everything that we've seen of the game so far, the DLSS departure doesn't seem to have had all that much negative impact on the finished result, but it's still a shame to see even Nintendo's biggest games missing out — particularly after all the DLSS hype in the console's reveal.

@AI-Generation FSR 1 is a very easy to drop in post rendering option, it’s so easy to drop in on the Steam Deck there’s a toggle to enable it for any game in the system menu. With DLSS and FSR 2 onwards the engine needs to provide motion vectors (how any objects through the scene are moving) so that can be taken into account to produce the superior result.

It made sense when Donkey Kong and Mario Kart (plus all the Switch 2 editions/patches except Pokemon Scarlet/Violet) didn’t include DLSS since it’s not trivial to add support for motion vectors for upscaling to something but I’m a bit puzzled as to why over a year later we still are seeing games using FSR 1 published by Nintendo.

Digital Foundry did a piece on Nintendos avoidance of DLSS and they theorised its likely down to the fact that:

Their 1st party games are using in-house engines which were built ground up for the Wii U era. Nintendos 1st foray into HD development. Said engines are incompatible with hardware accelerated upscalers like DLSS. They dont produce the vector information DLSS needs in their current state. This forces Nintendo to rely on software based upscalers like FSR.

Also some of these 1st party titles began development on Switch 1 (as Nintendo confirmed with MK World and DK Bananza) so again the underlying tech reflects that.

#4140. Honkai: Star Rail players are eating good, with Version 4.2 and third anniversary celebrations kicking off later this month

Honkai: Star Rail will be celebrating its third anniversary just days after it delivers a major update, and there's quite a bit to chew on in this one.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

As for the big third anniversary celebration, it will kick off in-game on April 26, bringing back Festive Gifts. The event will only be available during these celebrations, and it will once again be gifting players who log in regularly a total of 20 pulls.

You’ll also be able to a select a blessing card from a companion of your choice to receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. The same celebrations will also seeHuohuo and Robin permanently added to the Stellar Convergence store. You’ll have another chance to exchange a Golden Companion Spirit for any companion you like in that store, too — and all you need to do is log in anytime between Versions 4.2 and 4.4. This being a new year for Honkai: Star Rail, the top-up double bonus is resetting, meaning anyone who tops up their wallet will get a hefty bonus.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

#4139. Woim is the earth-guzzling, self-bisecting sokoban pick-me-up I needed after a week of games industry disasters

While ladling city-builders into the Maw's feeding trough this week, I remarked that being a worm must really suck. Then came the closure of BioWare, layoffs across other EA studios, further depressing genAI revelations, allegations of antisemitism at indie gaming events, a big Capcom data breach, and yet more worrying tidyings about Arkane.

I rescind my earlier observation: I would like to be a worm. A happy little worm, tunnelling after golden apples in the moist and forgiving earth, where there are no emails or press releases at all. The only thing I have to worry about down here is my butt growing so big I get stuck behind it. And also getting chopped in half by sliding doors, but it turns out this may actually help with the first problem. See for yourself - video below.

Ah, to be a soil-dwelling invertebrate in Woim, a puzzle game with a touch of the sokobans, consisting of 50 levels and an unspecified quantity of secrets, scattered across four subterranean worlds. The idea in each level is to crawl around a grid layout to reach a golden apple, opening the exit.

As with non-videogame worms, this involves a certain amount of ingesting earth and pooping it out behind you, but you can't just devour the whole layout. You'll need to guzzle red apples that make you longer, so that you can (for example) keep pressing a switch with your body as you slither towards a door. Or you might have to shove a rock onto that switch. Or shove that rock onto a water jet to propel it somewhere you can't reach.

Later on, there are breakable eggs that must be carried to nests, daisies that push back outward when you take your weight off them, scissors with which to snip yourself into separately functioning halves, and hats. I don't think this is an entirely accurate worm simulator. As in sokoban, the major problem is trapping yourself, but you can undo moves without penalty by tapping Z.

I've played six levels, and it's a jolly production. The music wobbles and boobles along, and your worm has a habit of looking at you expectantly when you get stuck that makes me giggle. Read more about it on Steam. If, unlike me, you've had a really uplifting week and are in sore need of a sokobanlike charged with maximum ontological dread, may I recommend Void Stranger.

Microsoft has revealed the next 14 games leaving Xbox Game Pass in early November 2026, with all of these being highlighted as "leaving soon" on the official Xbox phone app.

There are some pretty decent ones in here, including 1000xRESIST, Wreckfest, and the iconic GoldenEye 007, so it's well worth giving those a try before the middle of November if you haven't yet!

Football Manager 26 is leaving Xbox Game Pass on November 10th, whereas everything else is scheduled to depart on the 15th. You'll find discounts of at least 20% on most of these Xbox Game Pass titles until they leave the service.

#4137. Animal Crossing: New Horizons gets a new item to celebrate 25 years of the series

The allegedly finished game might finally, truly be feature complete with the addition of an anniversary item.

Animal Crossing: New Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The update, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

The patch brings a single new addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

After installing the patch, simply head to your in-house mailbox to claim it. The mail includes a hearty message to fans who supported the series for years, featuring an appropriate Nintendo N64 stamp.

The Leaf Statue, as it’s referred to in-game, lights up when placed.

April 14, 2011 marks the release of the original, lesser-known version of Animal Crossing in Japan. The game was initially released as Animal Forest (Dobutsu no Mori) on the Nintendo N64, before later making its way to the Nintendo GameCube in December of the same year as Dobutsu no Mori+ with some extra features.

That same, original design of the package is also available for display in your game. The rest of the patch notes are entirely about various bug fixes, so not much more there. You can see the full change log on Nintendo’s support website.

#4136. Stealth Classic Thief: The Dark Project Returns for a PS5 Remaster with New Content

One of the classics that helped create an entire genre, stealth masterpiece Thief: The Dark Project is coming to PS5 in remastered form next month, from 3rd December 2026.

This new version of the 1998 game has been remastered using Nightdive Studios' KEX Engine to produce a new edition running at 4K and 120 frames-per-second. It's got all the content of the base game, the three extra missions from Thief: Gold, and an entirely new campaign in the form of The Tarnished Mirror.

The Tarnished Mirror is a narrative bridge between The Dark Project and Thief 2: The Metal Age. In it, "a seemingly straightforward theft spirals into imprisonment, uneasy alliances and a descent into a drowned, R’lyeh-like necropolis. Players will experience an expanded enemy roster, ambitious level design and a pure Thief experience that descends into unsettling, otherworldly horror."

The bonus campaign has been created by the same people who made Thief: The Black Parade, which was a mod / expansion for Thief: Gold, made by the fans. "This collaboration marks a rare industry moment, with Nightdive and Eidos-Montréal welcoming a community creation directly into official canon," the press release added.

You can also expect the following from the remastered package:

Pre-orders are live on the PS Store for the PS5 digital versions, with a standard edition costing £24.99 / $29.99 and a Digital Deluxe Edition priced at £28.99 / $34.99.

In terms of physical editions, you're looking at three versions to choose from: standard, steelbook, and deluxe trapezoid. The first two are self-explanatory, but the Deluxe Trapezoid edition includes the game, steelbook, booklet, a box, and a physical remaster diary for £49.99 / $69.99:

Liam grew up with a PlayStation controller in his hands and a love for Metal Gear Solid. Nowadays, he's found playing the latest and greatest PS5 games as well as supporting Derby County. That last detail is his downfall.

#4135. Review: Marvel's Guardians Of The Galaxy: Encore Edition (Switch 2) - A Bright And Charming Adventure With An Okay Port

Marvel's Guardians of the Galaxy: Encore Edition

While cloud streaming has its benefits, nothing beats having a native version of a game. Guardians of the Galaxy launched on the first Nintendo Switch as a Cloud version, and that experience wasn’t really recommended. Now, the game is having an Encore Edition on Switch 2 with an actual port. It’s the same fun adventure, but with some performance caveats.

Guardians of the Galaxy follows Peter Quill as Star-Lord, as he travels the galaxy with his ragtag team of heroes: Rocket Raccoon, Drax, Groot, and Gamora. It starts out as a scrappy adventure of them trying to get out of debt, but eventually becomes much more engrossing and deeper as it progresses. It’s a story about friendship and teamwork that hits all the right notes.

As someone whose immediate frame of reference for this group is the Marvel Cinematic Universe rather than the comic books, I actually enjoyed this incarnation rather than their portrayal in the movies. The voice acting, script, and art direction are top-notch.

I already played the game once before on a different platform, but revisiting on Switch 2 felt like seeing an old friend again. I laughed at the interactions and jokes, as well as getting teary-eyed at the emotional scenes, as if witnessing them for the first time.

Unsurprisingly, the graphics have taken a small hit on Switch 2 compared to other platforms, but the gorgeous environmental and enemy designs more than make up for it. The different planets are alien, yet colourful, while enemy types are more plentiful than you’d think. From weird worms to gelatinous cubes, there’s enough wackiness to keep your eyes entertained.

While you only control Peter and his dual pistols during gameplay, you can deliver attack commands to the rest of the crew. For example, Drax can stagger bigger enemies while Rocket can clear huge areas with his explosives if you’re starting to get overwhelmed. It’s a little disappointing that you can’t play as other characters, but they all feel like they’re participating in some way.

Peter also unlocks different elemental shots throughout the campaign, giving him even more options. The Ice shot freezes foes in place, allowing you to inflict even more damage, while the Lightning shot can ricochet between nearby enemies. The combat isn’t particularly deep, but there’s more than enough variation to keep things fresh.

When building up a gauge, you can activate Huddle, where Peter gives a pep talk to his teammates to bolster their spirits. If you provide the correct response based on their mood, the whole team gets a temporary strength boost. Even if you pick incorrectly, Peter himself still gets the boost. This is also a clever way to show off the game’s fantastic soundtrack, filled with classic '70s and '80s jams like Rick Astley’s Never Gonna Give You Up and Europe’s The Final Countdown. The game is already bursting with charm and personality, and the music is the perfect cherry on top.

One of Peter’s many unlockable perks is an active-reload mechanic popularised by Gears of War. If you time your button presses correctly, Peter will reload immediately instead of having to wait, making it a satisfying minigame within the hectic combat. While my preferred way to play most Switch 2 games is with a Pro Controller, the constant rumbling when firing and the active-reload feel absolutely incredible on Joy-Con, and I eventually shifted to mainly playing with them.

The Switch 2 version includes two new control schemes in Gyroscope and Mouse Mode. The former lets you tilt your controller when you’re flying the group’s spaceship, the Milano, as well as guide Peter when he’s sliding or using his Jet Boots. The latter is just as you’d expect: you can use the right Joy-Con as a mouse to move the camera. There are no surprises here.

There are also new glam-rock-inspired skins for each of the main characters. I guess it’s a nice exclusive for the Encore Edition, but doesn’t impact the overall game.

This Switch 2 port’s performance is just…fine. While docked, the quality and performance modes target 30fps and 40fps, respectively. In handheld, it targets 30fps. Even in docked mode, there are hitches and stutters throughout the campaign. The loading times aren’t great either, and I booted up my PlayStation version from 2021 to compare. On that and the Switch 2, both loading screens last roughly 15 seconds, which can be quite annoying and noticeable. The bar is very low, but performance overall is still miles better than the Cloud version!

Also, credit where it's due, the Encore Edition has squished out a few bugs and glitches. A nasty one from other platforms was that certain conversations wouldn’t trigger when picking up collectibles if you decided to load up a previous save file. Thus the items wouldn’t show up in Peter’s glossary, which was a huge problem for completionists, and the feasible solution was to start a new game. After some testing, it seems like this particular glitch has thankfully been fixed in this version.

Guardians of the Galaxy was criminally overlooked when it first came out on other platforms. This single-player adventure is full of heart with equally fun gameplay to match. It’s also a shame that the disastrous Cloud version on the first Switch cast a large shadow on an otherwise stellar release.

But those dark days are over. If you can stomach some performance issues, this is one bright and resonating story you’ll want to experience at least once. Without the need of a constant internet connection, you can take Guardians of the Galaxy: Encore Edition outside in the sun, literally!

#4134. "This was not a Creative Assembly developed game": Total War boss points the finger at external partner for Shogun 2 Complete Edition disaster

But concedes that "we took our eyes off" its creation

Last week, Creative Assembly and Sega pulled Total War: Shogun 2's remastered Complete Edition from Steam, after an avalanche of complaints about technical problems and some AI-generated art. Now, Total War vice president Roger Collum has written a personal apology, while pinning some of the blame on an unnamed external partner. He's also clarified Creative Assembly's stance on generative AI, conceding that the studio do use it to help with "analysis, debugging, or speedy prototyping", but that they're against using it to generate game assets and art.

"I get many of you are angry and disappointed about the state of the Shogun 2: Complete Edition release," Collum writes on the official Twar Reddit. "We are too – especially the team members who have put everything into Total War games for years, some even decades. This was not a Creative Assembly developed game. It wasn’t subject to our same internal reviews and quality assurance. We took our eyes off its external development, with all our teams focused on our next big projects. However, whatever the development arrangements, Total War is our franchise and our name is on it."

Again, Collum doesn't name the external developer in question, but Mataboo Games are listed as co-devs on the Steam page. Collum says that SEGA and a small team of senior developers are working with the external team on "next steps", with details to follow. In the meantime, he has some general thoughts on how and when the Twarfolk make use of generative AI tools.

"I want to be very clear on the studio-wide stance on generative AI, because I know there are many questions about where we stand," Collum writes. "We are a craft studio. Our games are made by incredibly talented people, and we do not believe in a world where technology replaces the creativity of humans. At Creative Assembly we do not use generative AI to create game assets, including AI-generated art. We demand the same of any external developers we work with. The situation with Shogun 2: Complete Edition is being investigated."

Collum adds that Creative Assembly do, however, use AI tools for "support" purposes. "It shouldn’t replace the creator," he says. "I don’t believe that AI can replace the human experience, judgement and creativity that awesome experiences come from. Can AI tools help with analysis, debugging, or speedy prototyping so our experts can focus on making incredible games? Absolutely."

Collum ends his message by requesting that people don't abuse individual Total War developers. "Our community teams, QA, designers, and everyone in between are doing their job, as asked by the company," Collum writes. "Their safety is our priority. They do not deserve, and we will not tolerate, harassment or being singled out online and personally criticised." Collum warns that if you're nasty to developers, the studio may need to be less transparent in future.

I'm not sure I wholly buy the argument about "taking our eyes off" the game, given that Creative Assembly and Sega ran a bunch of trailers and marketing for it and sent round a FAQ detailing, among other things, how it would affect mods. While unavailable for purchase, the Complete Edition's Steam page is still live as of writing with "overwhelmingly negative" reviews. Creative Assembly and Sega have reinstated the original game's Steam page while they work on kicking the CE into shape.

#4133. Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

Metro 2039 takes us back to the tunnels of the Moscow Metro where, fittingly, Nazi ideology never died.

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

#4132. Xbox Black Friday Sale 2026 Leaks Early, Thousands Of Games Set To Be Included

We're still a little while away from Black Friday in late November, but Xbox is already preparing for a massive Black Friday sale in a few weeks' time, and the list of potential games has leaked online in recent days.

This is courtesy of a user named "Bloomy" over on the CheapAssGamer website, who says there are specifically 3,519 items in the list. The actual number of discounts is set to be lower than that though, as Bloomy breaks down each "Deluxe Edition" and similar bundles into individual items (some of which aren't purchasable on their own).

There's every chance the list could change between now and November 19th, which is seemingly the start date, but as things stand, the likes of 007 First Light, Ace Combat 8, Star Wars: Zero Company, The Blood of Dawnwalker and Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced look set to receive discounts as part of the sale.

We initially came across this via a post over on the official Xbox subreddit:

This certainly lines up with what we'd expect from the Xbox Black Friday Sale - last year's one began on November 20th (which, like this year's reported date, was also a Thursday) and included over 2000 games.

It's worth keeping in mind that Xbox may start providing discounts for accessories and potentially even consoles (you never know!) before the game-focused sale begins on the 19th, so keep an eye out for those as well.

Naturally, you'll be able to find all the Xbox Black Friday 2026 game deals and their prices on Pure Xbox as soon as the sale begins in mid-November, but you might need to bear with us as it's set to begin on the release date for GTA 6!

#4131. Travis Touchdown 'Will Definitely Be Back' for No More Heroes 20th Anniversary

Goichi Suda (aka Suda51), head honcho of developer Grasshopper Manufacture, has given fans fresh hope of more to come for the cult favourite No More Heroes series.

Speaking to Famitsu as part of a wider interview, he's asked about No More Heroes as it's approaching its 20th anniversary in 2027.

Asked if there's anything being planned for the occasion, Suda51 says his team and publisher Marvelous are indeed cooking up something. (Quotations machine translated.)

"Marvelous is aware of this, so we definitely want to do something together for the 20th anniversary," he says. "We're planning to deliver something special, so please look forward to it. Travis Touchdown will definitely be back!"

He didn't provide any further details, but it sounds like there's something for fans to look forward to in the new year.

The original No More Heroes was released in Japan in December 2007, and was later brought to western audiences in 2008.

There have been several games in the series, with the latest being No More Heroes 3, released for PS5 and PS4 in 2022.

Anyway, there's not a lot to go on here, but it seems fans of the franchise have got something to look forward to in the near future.

Are you excited to see what Suda51 has planned for No More Heroes' 20th anniversary? Tell us in the comments section below.

#4130. BioWare staff "should be given the first opportunity and the federal support" to buy the studio and keep it running, says Canadian political party leader

Hope. It's in short supply at the moment. Regardless, I hope that something a Canadian politician's proposed in a post scoring easy likeability points at the expense of EA's recently installed owners comes to pass, no matter how unlikely it is to do so at this point. Rather than being unceremoniuously shuttered, leaving the world staring down the barrel of a future without new games from a storied studio, BioWare should be handed over to its staff with backing from the Canadian government.

Nationalise BioWare, basically. Well, sort of. "The developers at BioWare know how to run the studio," is what Avi Lewis, leader of Canada's New Democratic Party, wrote in a post following the closure. "They know how to make the games we all love. They should be given the first opportunity - and the federal support - to buy it and run it themselves. And if we want to avoid the Mass Effect effect in Canada, we should be keeping private equity out, not welcoming it in."

You can almost hear the horde of suit-wearing money-knowers who've sensed that suggestion's been made and are about to descend from orbit to yell about taxpayers' money being used to help ensure the creation of future adventures starring space blokes who say 'We'll bang, ok?'. I should also point out that since I'm not Canadian, it wouldn't be the country I live in spending some of their cash on helping the Veilguard avoid being veilgone to the depths of the vault where EA keep Burnout and ten million other defunct series people would like to see return.

The developers at BioWare know how to run the studio. They know how to make the games we all love. They should be given the first opportunity - and the federal support - to buy it and run it themselves.

In all seriousness, I'm not totally sure it'd work out in the long run, but it's something. An alternative to a company erasing a studio from existence because the Saudi Public Investment Fund and Jared Kushner have been allowed to load them up with a ton of debt rather than reaching further into their own pockets.

So, I say screw it. Set up a new position called Minister for BioWare to ensure the devs have what they need to get their heads down that next Mass Effect which reportedly had a trailer leak the other day. Just make sure it's not some right-wing crank, or BioWare might run into some of the same problems it'd been feared their generally very inclusive games might face under Saudi ownership.
